anomalies.observed: USB4 D+ (via R50) is routed to FCC2 pin 72 (PA13, the SWDIO/JTMS pin). USB4 D- (via R46) is routed to FCC2 pin 71 (PA12). The ID line (via R20) is on FCC2 pin 70 (PA11). The USB full-speed data pins are therefore not on the MCU's dedicated USB DP/DM pins.
anomalies.expected: On STM32 full-speed USB, DM is PA11 and DP is PA12. D+ should sit on PA12 and D- on PA11. PA13 is the SWD data line and cannot carry USB D+.
anomalies.impact: USB enumeration on the USB4 port would fail because D+ and D- are on the wrong MCU pins. The PA13 connection also loads the SWD data line.

anomalies.observed: PCA9685 A0 (pin 1) is tied to the +3.3V net, while A1–A5 (pins 2, 3, 4, 5, 24) are all tied to GND. This sets the address bit high.
anomalies.expected: The specification lists the PCA9685PW at I2C address 0x40, which requires A0 to be low like the other address pins.
anomalies.impact: The PWM driver would respond at 0x41 instead of 0x40, so firmware addressing the servo driver at 0x40 would get no response. The spec also places the INA219 at 0x40 on the same FCC bus, so the strapping may be deliberate; this is a low-confidence finding.
